gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Tall, pressed-flat bowls keep Noto Sans Grantha moving without a snag in the line. Grandstander does bold, expressive display work best, while Noto Sans Grantha handles the plain sans job of staying out of the way.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-gujarat: Noto Sans Gujarati draws curved strokes that stop before they turn inward, leaving big open counters. Noto Sans Gujarati sits quietly under Grandstander's chunky, hairline-free headings, so the loud and the clear each get their own space.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Chunky, crayon-tall, and cheerfully loud. Grandstander brings bold, expressive lines of constant width, and Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi gives them a modern sans partner whose terminals cut back to leave generous gaps.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Grandstander is bold and expressive, drawn with flat, unmodulated lines and a tall x-height. Noto Sans Hebrew follows with a dominant midsection and wide gaps between curves and stems, so a longer passage moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-hk: Grandstander is bold and expressive, with diagonals as thick as its horizontals and short ascenders. Noto Sans HK follows with large lowercase forms and brush ends lifted before curves close, so a longer passage reads cleanly and steadily.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-imperia: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads friendly and sturdy, its c ends pointing apart like open pincers. Over a longer passage that short step from lowercase to capital height keeps the rhythm gentle, while Grandstander's bold headings stay uniform in every stroke direction.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-inscrip: Expressive is the first word for Grandstander, drawn with a unit-width stroke throughout. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian brings big open eyes and a deep middle band, and shrinking the heading would blunt its boldness.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-jp: Tall, sweeping, and confident from top to bottom, with Grandstander's rounds and stems in one weight. Noto Sans JP's very tall x-height is the shared strength here.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Grandstander looks like neon tubing bent into letters of constant thickness. Noto Sans Kaithi does the opposite job best, filling the line with an open-channel e and lowercase forms that stand almost like capitals.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Approachable describes Noto Sans Kannada, with a gentle bump up from small letters to capitals and s curves opening wide at both ends. Grandstander's bold, calligraphy-free outlines sit above it comfortably.
